valuation_philosophy: Mainfreight is a founder-led, capital-intensive global logistics compounder that has historically traded at a genuine premium NZX multiple (avg P/E ~26x, P/B ~3.9x, EV/EBITDA ~11.2x ex the FY2022/23 freight-rate super-spike). This DCF deliberately does NOT clip the intrinsic value up to that premium: it is a cash-flow-based fair value built from through-cycle, component-level assumptions (owner FCF after mandatory IFRS16 lease-principal repayment, EBITDA margin recovering only to its historical ex-spike average, capex held near the FY2027-guided level rather than assumed to taper away). The result is a base-case intrinsic value ($39.02) well BELOW the current price ($69.01), which is the DCF's honest statement that the market is paying, and has long paid, a premium for the quality of the franchise (owner-operator culture, NZ/Australia network density, multi-decade compounding record) that a pure owner-FCF model does not capture. The Step 8c sanity check confirms this is not a modelling error: all three implied multiples at the base IV (P/E 15.6x, P/B 1.8x, EV/EBITDA 5.1x) sit comfortably BELOW Mainfreight's own historical trading range, so if anything the model is conservative relative to history, not aggressive. Investors should read this as 'quality compounder trading at a persistent premium to owner-FCF fair value' rather than 'DCF says sell' — the premium itself is the market's price for the moat. FY2026 is also a soft-patch year (PBT -8.5%, H1 PBT -18.3%) inside a freight-rate downturn, which further widens the price/DCF gap versus a scenario where the market is pricing an expected H2/FY2027 recovery that hasn't yet shown up in trailing owner FCF.

inputs.sbc_note: SBC is VERIFIED NIL for Mainfreight (10-K/annual report footnotes confirm no share-based payment expense since FY2019; only a trivial $55k in FY2017; StockBasedComp column is 0.0 for all 20 periods in the Metrics CSV). The SBC adjustment step is therefore a genuine no-op here, not a skipped step -- there is nothing to deduct and nothing to dilute. Share count has been static at 100,698,548 since FY2017 (no buybacks needed because there is no dilution to offset).
inputs.lease_adjustment_note: IFRS16 lease principal repayment is deducted from reported FCF to reach owner FCF, because Mainfreight is a large-scale property/warehouse/vehicle lessee and this is a genuine recurring non-discretionary cash outflow that the reported OCF-minus-capex FreeCashFlow figure excludes. FY2026: reported FCF 392.09 - lease principal 209.505 = owner FCF 182.59 (53% haircut). Applied across FY2020-FY2026 (the IFRS16-adopted period); pre-FY2020 years had operating lease rent embedded in opex instead, so the pre/post series is not perfectly comparable and CAGRs spanning the transition should be read with that caveat. Consequently, IFRS16 lease liabilities (~NZ$1.29bn) are EXCLUDED from net debt to avoid double-counting the same lease obligation as both a cash outflow (in FCF) and a balance-sheet liability (in net debt) -- net debt uses bank/asset-finance TotalDebt only.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income was only $3.3m against a net CASH position of just $26.6m (net cash is far below 1x the FCF base) -- immaterial, so no interest-income strip was applied to avoid an inconsequential double-adjustment.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/annual report footnotes; StockBasedComp column in Metrics CSV (0.0 all periods)
inputs.net_debt_basis: Bank/asset-finance TotalDebt (135.549) less Cash (162.189) = net CASH -26.64. IFRS16 lease liabilities deliberately excluded (see lease_adjustment_note) to avoid double-counting the lease obligation already captured as a cash outflow in owner FCF.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_9yr_through_cycle_cagr (FY2017->FY2026, a full freight cycle including both the COVID super-spike and its unwind)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (14.2% through-cycle) diverges materially above Revenue CAGR (9.7%) and EPS CAGR (10.5%). This is NOT SBC-driven dilution-avoidance (SBC is nil) -- it is retained-earnings compounding on a static share count with zero buybacks and zero dividends-out-of-capital, i.e. equity simply accumulates faster than revenue because margins expanded structurally post-IFRS16 (EBITDA margin ~8.5% pre-IFRS16 vs ~13-15% post-IFRS16, an accounting-driven step change, not organic margin gain) and because FY2022/23 windfall profits were retained rather than distributed. Revenue CAGR is used as the primary growth driver instead of equity CAGR because it is the cleanest, least distorted through-cycle series and is directly tied to the volume/branch-density growth drivers in the qualitative analysis.
historical_growth.notes: 3yr CAGRs (FY23->FY26) are all negative because FY2023 was the peak of the COVID freight-rate super-spike (revenue $5,675.7m, EBITDA $851.0m, NPAT $426.5m) -- using FY2023 as a CAGR start point systematically understates growth. The 9-10yr through-cycle CAGRs (FY2017->FY2026) are used instead as they span a full up-cycle and down-cycle. Owner FCF CAGR cannot be cleanly computed pre/post IFRS16 (lease principal repayment is 0 pre-FY2020 as operating leases sat in opex instead), so the FY2020->FY2026 6yr owner-FCF CAGR (28.7%) is shown for reference only and not used as a growth driver -- it is distorted by FY2020 being an unusually low owner-FCF base (COVID-affected, high capex year, only 1.30% owner-FCF margin).

base.rationale: Growth reaccelerates gradually off the FY2026 soft patch (revenue +2.8% reported, -0.2% constant-currency) toward but below the 9.7% through-cycle CAGR, reflecting continued freight-rate softness offset by NZ/Australia network intensification. EBITDA margin recovers modestly from FY2026's 14.11% (H2 already showed cost-discipline improvement per management commentary) toward the post-IFRS16 ex-spike average (~14.5%), not the FY2022/23 spike level (13.6-15.0%, itself already close to this range so no aggressive assumption). Capex held near the FY2027-guided $234m level (~4.3% of revenue) rather than tapering, per management's stated continued heavy capex programme (further $102m of FY2028 property capex flagged). Cash tax rate held flat at the FY2020-26 average (~27-28%), which is already close to NZ's 28% statutory rate -- no abnormal one-off to ramp away.

bull.rationale: Europe/Americas networks inflect to sustained profitability (bull case in analysis JSON), Australia's profit lead over NZ widens, freight-rate cycle recovers faster than base case, and the $10bn FY2029/30 revenue aspiration is broadly on track. EBITDA margin approaches the FY2024/25 levels (15.3%/14.5%) sustainably rather than as a cyclical peak.

bear.rationale: Global freight-rate downturn persists (ocean rates forecast to fall further into 2026 on overcapacity), Europe/Americas losses continue for longer without inflection, cost-discipline lag from FY2026 H1 repeats, and FX/tariff disruption weighs on constant-currency growth. Lower terminal cap multiple (12x vs 15x base) reflects the cyclical/structurally-slower-growth character this scenario implies.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC (8.5%-12.5%), columns = terminal growth (1.25%-3.25%), base-case FCF path. Top-right cells flatten at the 15x terminal-FCF cap ($48.61 = 15 x FY5 owner FCF $367.32 / shares, discounted and added to PV of interim FCF) once Gordon growth would otherwise exceed it at low WACC/high terminal growth combinations.

historical_multiples_table.outlier: freight-rate super-spike peak year, excluded from averages

sanity_check.multiples_note: P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA computed at the March close nearest each FY-end (31 March fiscal year), unadjusted for SBC (SBC is verified nil for Mainfreight so no SBC adjustment is needed for like-for-like comparison with the DCF, which is also built on a zero-SBC basis). These will not exactly match Yahoo/screener GAAP multiples due to minor EPS/EBITDA definitional differences but are directionally consistent.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trips. All three implied multiples at the base-case intrinsic value ($39.02) sit well BELOW Mainfreight's own historical trading range: implied P/E 15.65x vs 26.25x historical average (40% below, not above); implied P/B 1.84x vs 6.27x historical maximum (71% below); implied EV/EBITDA 5.14x vs 15.20x historical maximum (66% below). The large negative base-case upside (-43.5%) is therefore NOT a sign of an inflated DCF -- it reflects that Mainfreight has consistently traded at a premium to a conservative owner-FCF valuation throughout its listed history, which is consistent with the qualitative analysis's own framing of a persistently premium-rated, founder-led compounder. No fix was required or applied.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None -- sanity check passed on first construction.
